danny.audio_profile: Danny, late thirties, with a deep, rough, gravelly voice. He's worn out and still shaken, and he tells it slowly and plainly in his own natural voice, with little inflection, like a real person remembering something awful, not an actor.

scene: Late at night, a tired man who hasn't slept since that night sits at a microphone and slowly tells what happened in the first hour of a zombie outbreak at the mall where he works. He takes his time, with small pauses where it still gets to him. Plain and natural, no music.
sample_context: A first-person story told slowly and plainly, in a deep, rough, shaken voice.

lines.text: Right now there's a zombie pressed up against my gate, and it's wearing my best friend's uniform.
The radio on his chest is about to tell every one of them exactly where I'm hiding.
An hour ago, I was basically the king of this mall.
Let me back up.
I'm Danny. I do night security at Maplecrest Mall, and yeah, I've heard every mall cop joke there is.
I work nights for one reason. At three-fifteen every afternoon, I'm standing at the bus stop when my daughter Lily gets off.
She's seven, and she thinks I'm the king of the mall, because I carry forty-two keys, one for every store.
Tonight, I'd only need one of them.
The job's pretty simple. I walk the loop, I rattle the gates, and around one a.m., Marcus calls me from down in the parking garage.
Marcus is twenty-two, he's studying to be a nurse, and he tells the worst jokes you've ever heard.
Tonight he calls at one-forty, and there's no joke. He's whispering.
